# Stow

> Embeddable object storage for applications, tests and ephemeral workloads.
> One object model through an in-process Go/WASM runtime or a native S3
> endpoint, with portable workspaces and browser persistence when you need them.

Stow is an Apache 2.0 object engine with native S3 HTTP compatibility and a
WebAssembly profile. Prepared filesystem workspaces support checkpoints,
comparison, and portable handoff. The browser profile offers IndexedDB
persistence, retained file stages, undo/redo, and explicit conditional sync
through host-supplied networking. Embedded Go and Node WASM runtimes need no
HTTP listener. Native run-through mode adds an S3 read-through cache with
prewarming, cache limits, TTL, and explicit offline operation. WASM enables
embedding in compatible hosts; edge platform integrations need qualification.
Stow owns storage; the host owns execution and sandbox enforcement.

Native live writes commit locally before propagation through a durable outbox.
The outbox preserves the exact version, retries transient failures with bounded
backoff, and stops on remote conflicts or an unknown upstream baseline. Recovery
checks the remote ETag, content type, metadata, and requested checksum before
acknowledging an attempted write. Retry and discard require the admin token.

## Start here

- [API reference](/docs/api/): public Go, TypeScript and Python declarations, methods, defaults and errors.

- [Browser file history and sync](/docs/browser-file-history/):
  local commit, undo/redo, conditional writes, recovery, and limits.
- [Real browser editor demo](/docs/browser-editor/):
  run `make browser-editor` from a built source checkout.
- [Native read-through cache](/docs/run-through/):
  cache reads, prewarm exact keys, and work offline.
- [Durable outbox contract](/docs/s3-compatibility/#62-read-through-cache-semantics):
  local-first writes, conditional propagation, retries, and crash recovery.

- [Agent instructions](/agent.md): install commands, the prepared workspace
  flow for coding tasks, and the scoped-session pattern for disposable S3.
- [Running and probing a server](/docs/server/):
  how to start `stow-s3` yourself, read the endpoint and credentials it actually
  got, probe `/_stow/health`, and avoid the port and mode traps. Read this before
  writing a launcher.
- [Task manifest guide](/docs/task-manifests/): manifest fields, lifecycle, checkpoints, archives, and isolation limits.
- [Full reference](/docs/reference/):
  the full reference, including the CLI, the Go runtime, and the WebAssembly
  profile.

## Install

Native v0.3.2 binaries for Linux and macOS are distributed through
[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/chester-hill-solutions/stow-s3/releases/tag/v0.3.2).
Verify the archive with the release checksum manifest and run `stow-s3 --version`.
npm and PyPI publication are deferred; use source checkouts for those clients.


The 0.3.2 TypeScript and Python clients are not yet published. Use a source checkout.
The Go module is published. Native package targets are Linux and macOS on x64 and arm64.
Use WSL on Windows.

```bash
go get github.com/chester-hill-solutions/stow-s3/pkg/stow   # Go, works now
```

TypeScript and Python work from a source checkout: `git clone`, `make build`,
then `export STOW_BIN="$PWD/bin/stow-s3"`, then `npm install && npm run build`
in `packages/stow-s3` (TypeScript) or `pip install -e
"packages/stow-s3-py[boto3]"` (Python). A published package carries its own
binary and does not need `STOW_BIN`.
If the binary cannot be found or run, `stow-s3 doctor` reports which side is
broken.
